note: Hand-written. Everything measured (fixtures, fidelity, behaviour, confidence, detection counts) is NOT here: tools/formats/build-db.mjs reads it from tests/results/scorecard.json and the fixture manifests. This file holds what a measurement cannot say: what was changed because of a failure, the failure patterns that remain, and what is assumed and not shown. Every improvement names the file that holds it and the test that keeps it.

research: README and git history read as text; the three revisions were then run in tests/corpus/tools/sandbox_run.py (no network, no host files) through gen_obscura.py

improvements.summary: math.floor / math.ceil of an integer literal is the literal (the number layer wraps every number in it), so bit32.bxor(math.floor(a), math.floor(b)) folds and the control-flow flattener's next states become constants
a closure called on the spot that only computes a constant from constants is that constant (the opaque predicates `(function() local n = 22 return n * n < 0 end)()`)
tests: tests/formats-ix.test.mjs: simplify: a closure called on the spot

improvements.summary: a flattened function inside another function's body is unflattened: a leaf that returns or raises the `error("CFF Error: Invalid state")` else no longer counts against the machine, and a loop of two blocks that cannot end on its own is read (closes KNOWN-ISSUES 27 for this shape)
a table of untouched globals read only by constant keys (the table-indirection layer, also `math.pi`) is inlined, whatever its name looks like; a numeric statement nobody keeps (`math.cos(12)`) goes
tests: tests/formats-ix.test.mjs: simplify: a table of builtins

improvements.summary: the run of executor-detection ifs at the top (1.1.0: empty error; 1.0.x: "Security violation" messages, in a do block) is taken off when at least two are present and one probes an executor-only global

lightweight mode decrypts its string table in place (`T[k] = D(T[k], key, i)`): the decoder call is seeded with the stored text, evaluated, and the reads and the copies the obfuscator made (`local a = T[1]`) become the strings
a function that reads or slices a string, mixes it with bxor and builds text with string.char is a decoder from its first call, however it is wrapped (a script with two hidden strings has two calls)
the reference-runtime oracle no longer dies on a recovered file whose report header holds a real Unicode character (it used to take every later request with it)

what is inside a VM that was not lifted: the function records (instruction bytes, parameters, registers), and the constants, read by running only the statements that set them up in the sandbox (never the interpreter); the hardened 1.1.0 build keeps its constants in keyed per-function records, which are opened one record at a time after the set-up loop that salts each record with the hash of its code. Reported in the output header as a profile, never as a recovery

the plain VM build (1.0.1 and 1.1.0) is lifted back to source: every handler of the build's own interpreter is taken apart into the operands it reads and a canonical body (names by first appearance, operands by first use, so a build that shuffles its operand order writes the same text) and recognised against a template list; the program's functions are decoded with the script's own key, boxes become the variables they stand for, byte jumps become instruction jumps, and the Lua 5.1 chunk goes to the decompiler that reads IronBrew 2 and Hercules. Every one of the 13 plain builds reads completely (no handler left unrecognised); where the tool's own output is right the lifted program runs like the original on Luau (7 of 7 in 1.1.0, 2 of 2 in 1.0.1)

failurePatterns.summary: the hardened builds (vm-max, vm-cached; 1.1.0, and 1.0.1 vm-max) are profiled, not lifted: they keep instruction bytes encrypted per function record (rolling PRNG, salted with the hash of the record), choose an operand order and a byte order per operation, dispatch through a tree of range tests instead of a flat chain, and fuse several operations into one generated handler (BLOCKn). The plain vm build is lifted since Prompt XI (improvements/vm-lift)
failurePatterns.evidence: tests/obscura-vm.test.mjs (hardened builds are reported as not lifted); docs/AUDIT.md (vm-max, vm-cached: semantic 2% to 4%, complete 0)

failurePatterns.summary: identifier renaming is not reversible: samples whose original names are descriptive (s02, s03, s06) lose fidelity that no pass can win back; the structure is recovered
failurePatterns.evidence: the remaining differences in s02/s03/s06 are names and inlined named constants

failurePatterns.summary: Obscura 1.0.0 fails with a Lexer error on one sample (s03); recorded as tool-error in its manifest, never counted as a recovery

four of the six 1.0.1 VM outputs (s02, s04, s05, s06) do not behave like the original program even on the reference runtime. s05 shows why: the compiler places a numeric loop's variable one register above where the FORLOOP handler writes it (the lifted program reads an unset register), and the VM itself fails earlier with a different error. The lifted program follows the bytecode; it is not expected to match an output the tool got wrong, and those fixtures are not judged

improvements.summary: the program kept as an array of scaled character codes (`_(99900)`, scale = a random number drawn at build time) is read by finding the scale that makes every entry divide and the text parse; the wrapper (globals table, tamper check, clock-seeded generator) goes
`string.char(d(n))` where d is a XOR with a key (the encrypt option, through `bit or bit32 or require'bit'`) is evaluated in the sandbox; `table.concat{ ... }` of the results folds to the string

the constants of the program (numbers, strings, booleans, `[k] = nil` where the program had nil) kept in one table written key by key are read back as the constants and the table goes; XFuscator default / uglify / nostep2 / notamper s02 and s06 went from fidelity 0.48 / 0.60 to 0.76 / 1.00 (the s02 remainder is the names, which the tool drops by design)

failurePatterns.summary: the precompile step reads Lua 5.1 bytecode through LAT, which reads every integer as a size_t: it only works on 32-bit builds. This host is 64-bit, so no precompiled output was generated and none is claimed
the tool itself fails with those options (Step2.lua:11 concatenates nil, init.lua:110 indexes nil): recorded as tool-error
locals are renamed (s02, s05, s06 lose their descriptive names)

assumptions: Output of XFuscator 2013 'Version 2.0 b1' only; there are 8 commits and the last one was run

research: README and examples/obfuscator-example.lua read as text; run through run_isolated.py with drivers/luaxen.lua (the call the example makes)

improvements.summary: numbers hidden as `setmetatable({}, {__op = function(_, a) local x, y, z = a[1], a[2], a[3] return x*x - y*y + z end}) <op> {x, y, z}` are evaluated without running anything; the same trick with a loop that builds strings from triples is evaluated in the sandbox when every name in it is declared inside or a standard global
a `while` whose body always leaves it is an `if` (the AST stage writes its conditionals this way)
the state loops of the AST stage (`while 0.69 do if state == ...`, as few as two blocks) are unflattened

the IronBrikked VM (base-36 LZW bytes: constants, instructions with mode and opcode bytes, nested functions; an opcode tree over Lua's own 38 operations plus an expansion by constant/register operands) is read from the script and lifted, alone and under the LuaXen syntax layer (14 of 14 fixtures lifted and structured). It is NOT claimed to run like the original: the generator's own output errors on all 14, its compiler writes counts the program did not have (results of calls, returns, method calls without their object) and its SETGLOBAL / SETUPVAL / TEST / TFORLOOP handlers read the wrong fields. The lifter reads each as the instruction it stands for, repairs the result count of calls from the registers read afterwards, and the confidence is capped

failurePatterns.summary: IronBrikked, the VM stage (LZW-compressed encoded prototype and an interpreter), is identified and reported as not recovered; with `both` the AST layer over it is peeled and the VM remains
the tool raised `No loop to break` on s04 in both configurations; recorded as tool-error

the tool's own IronBrikked output (14 fixtures, with and without the AST layer) does not run on any reference runtime available here: Lua 5.1, 5.2 and LuaJIT stop inside the generated VM with "attempt to compare nil with number" (the generated wrapper masks it as "LuaXen: (internal)"; the real message was read by replacing that string in a copy), Lua 5.3 / 5.4 have no math.ldexp, Luau stops with "attempt to call a nil value". They are excluded from runtime judgement, not counted for or against the engine

calls whose results are used are written with a result count of 0 or 1, RETURN carries a count that is not the number of values, a method call loses its object, a forward jump of 256 or more reads as a backward one: runs error; lifted output follows the encoded instructions and does not run like the original (the audit status is partial: structure and semantic gains are measured, runtime is not judged because the tool’s own output does not run)

assumptions: Only the single commit of the repository was run; `legacy/` was not touched

The tool's own output was NOT verified on the reference runtimes (the verification did not finish inside its budget, twice, including for the AST stage); `toolOutputVerified` is 0, so the behaviour rows for LuaXen compare the recovered script with the original program only, and nothing is claimed about the obfuscated file itself

research: README, Main.lua, Pipeline.lua and the Vm tree read as text; run through run_isolated.py with drivers/zartha.lua, which does in memory what Pipeline.lua does (luac replaced by string.dump)

improvements.summary: every build (default, minify, encryptstrings, flatten, antitamper, constants, all; 54 fixtures) is lifted back to Lua 5.1 instructions and decompiled: each function's dispatch is evaluated for every value of the counter (the control-flow-flattening predicates fold), the scratch-cell indirection is resolved, the text of each piece is recognised as the instruction it was made from, the upvalue maps become the MOVE / GETUPVAL words after CLOSURE, constants are decoded with the script's own decryptor and shift, parameters are read from what the code does. 39 builds (every build whose strings are readable) behave like the ORIGINAL program on Lua 5.1, among them 8 whose own output prints a wrong list of primes and 15 where it errors or does not finish; 15 builds mask strings with a per-constant key the generator never stores and are reported as not recoverable

the generator's SETGLOBAL stores the name instead of the value and its LOADBOOL reads a scratch cell it never wrote, so builds that use them do not run like the program; the lifter reads them as the instruction they were made from (the register is the one number nothing read; the boolean is the test written next to the cell). Its LOADBOOL template also writes `\n\t` as text, which makes the script invalid Lua (s06): only that text is mended, and the report says so

failurePatterns.summary: a per-build Lua 5.1 bytecode VM with generated opcodes: identified (watermark and the `Env["string"]["char"]` prelude) and flagged as not recovered; no lifter was written
luasrcdiet inside the tool fails on s06 in both configurations that minify (an unexpected backslash); recorded as tool-error

on s06 the tool writes `\n\t` as literal characters into the code of one opcode handler, which PUC Lua 5.1 and LuaJIT reject ("unexpected symbol near '\'"); QuickSilver's parser rejects it too, so those outputs are counted as unparsed, not as recovery failures

measured on Lua 5.1 and LuaJIT in an isolated runner with a wall-clock limit: 16 of 54 outputs behave like the original, 8 do not (s01 and s02 in default / minify / encryptstrings / flatten: the compiled program prints a wrong list of primes and nil where the original prints booleans), antitamper stops no run within 15 s, constants and all fail with "attempt to call field ?" (a nil value), and s06 / s08 are rejected by the runtime. None of these is counted against the engine

Strong/Medium s02 and s04 went from medium to high with structure 0.55 -> 0.74

backlog.state: 11 of 15 identified by structure; 4 remain unidentified
backlog.detail: the 15 files were read one by one: 11 are Luraph 14.x-shaped VMs without their banner (a returned table of short-named handlers with 0X / 0B literals, or the LPH_ build-flag macros) and are now identified by those two structural rules (flagged unrecoverable); the other 4 are not Luraph VMs (two request-function scripts, a hub script, a plain script) and are classified, not identified. backlog.item: Per-build bytecode VMs (Obscura VM, Zartha, FusGato, IronBrikked, RealObfuscator vm)
backlog.state: Zartha and FusGato lifted (Prompt XII); IronBrikked, RealObfuscator vm identified, not recovered
backlog.detail: each is flagged unrecoverable so that the report cannot say "recovered"; none has a lifter. Since Prompt X the Obscura VM (all three revisions, plain and hardened) has a profile of its data (functions, instruction bytes, decrypted constants; on all 39 Obscura VM fixtures every string of two or more characters of the original program is among the constants read: recall 1.00, `categories.vmConstants` in the database), shown in the report as NOT lifted

backlog.item: A lifter that rebuilds source from Obscura VM bytecode
backlog.state: plain Obscura VM, Zartha and FusGato done; hardened Obscura, IronBrikked, RealObfuscator vm not started
backlog.detail: the Obscura lifter reads each build's handlers from its own interpreter and decodes with its own key (src/recover/obscura-vm.js). The hardened Obscura builds additionally need: the instruction bytes opened in the sandbox (they are encrypted per record), an operand reader per byte order and offset style, the tree of range tests flattened to its leaves, and the fused BLOCK handlers split back into the operations they were made from. Zartha, FusGato and IronBrikked are different formats and need their own handler readers.

backlog.item: MoonVeil 2.0.26: the table of factories joined into one program
backlog.state: done for 2.0.26; 2.1.0 is a different design
backlog.detail: 2.0.26 does not keep its program as bytecode: it is a table of control-flow-flattened factories that build each other through a context object. They are now put back together (src/recover/moonveil-join.js): reference structure 0.2% -> 67%, fidelity 21% -> 34% on the one hand-made reference. 2.1.0 samples are a bytecode VM again (a serialized program run by a new interpreter whose outer function takes two parameters and whose inner takes none); the VM reader's first check, written for 2.0.25, stops there ("the interpreter does not have the expected shape")

backlog.item: Luraph version from structure, without a banner
backlog.detail: leave-one-out over the 198 labelled files of the public collection: the era (13 and earlier / 14.0-14.3 / 14.4-14.5 / 14.6-14.9 / 15+) is named correctly 78% of the time, the exact version 37%, the major.minor 51%. Minor revisions share their templates, so no rule can read the version reliably; the experiment is tools/research/luraph-era.mjs and its numbers data/research/luraph-era-eval.json

backlog.item: Zartha: a generated VM of per-instruction code lifted back to source
backlog.state: done; constant-protection strings are not recoverable
backlog.detail: src/recover/zartha-vm.js. 54 of 54 fixtures lifted and decompiled; the 39 builds with readable strings behave like the original program on Lua 5.1 (checked with the reference runtime, not with the sandbox); 15 mask their strings. Generic work it needed: an open call chain is part of a condition, the results of a call nothing named are written out before a condition (stripped chunks only), globals and methods whose names are not identifiers, a table of constants that is only read

backlog.item: FusGato: what it is, from reading its output
backlog.detail: an IronBrew 2 fork with a bit-string container (instruction words of 26 bits: A, B, C, no opcode) and an interpreter that is `if pc == n` with the handler of instruction n written out and its operands read from the decoded table; the leaf reader of the Zartha lifter plus a container reader lift it (src/recover/fusgato-vm.js). Evidence is two programs only
